page: Amazon Web Services r8i.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs with a dedicated allocation, running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The processor includes a massive 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations. It is equipped with 1536.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core.

In benchmark evaluations, the r8i.metal-48xl demonstrates top-tier performance across multi-core and memory-intensive workloads. The server achieves top-tier status in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU tests. Its memory subsystem delivers exceptional throughput, with read-only large block memory bandwidth reaching 585.17 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 232.99 GB/sec. Database operations are highly optimized, as evidenced by a top-tier Passmark database score and Redis SET performance reaching 296.12 million operations per second. Additionally, the platform excels in LLM inference tasks, processing prompts at 300.83 tokens/sec for medium 7B models and 42.05 tokens/sec for large 70B models.

The instance features a baseline network bandwidth of 75 Gbps, facilitating high-throughput data transfers. However, it does not include local NVMe storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes. Given its bare-metal nature, massive DDR5 memory capacity, and high-performance multi-core capabilities, the r8i.metal-48xl is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise-grade database operations, heavy multi-threaded compilation, and CPU-based machine learning or LLM inference workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services r8i.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server designed for resource-intensive enterprise workloads. It features 192 vCPUs across 96 physical Intel Xeon 6975P-C cores running at 3.9 GHz, paired with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory. The architecture supports advanced vector and matrix extensions (AVX-512 and AMX), driving top-tier multi-core and memory bandwidth performance. Benchmarks show exceptional capabilities in database operations, with Redis SET performance reaching 296.12 million operations per second, and strong LLM prompt processing speeds. While the server lacks local storage, its 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth ensures efficient connectivity to network storage. This instance is highly suited for in-memory databases, large-scale data processing, and complex multi-threaded enterprise applications.
